title.narrative: Education for sustainable development in West Africa

description.narrative: Countries in the West African sub-region are committed to achieving the goals of SDG4, including those of SDG4.7 on education for sustainable development. These countries recognize the transformative potential of ESD in education systems, equipping learners, children, youth and adults, with the knowledge, values, skills, attitudes and behaviours needed to make sustainable lifestyle choices. These countries adhere to the prescriptions of UNESCO's "ESD for 2030" Roadmap, which recommends structuring ESD interventions around five priority areas of action: (1) Policies, (2) Learning environments, (3) Capacity building for educators, (4) Youth and (5) Local action. At the beginning of 2026, nearly half of the states in the sub-region have expressed their interest, but the number of countries that successfully engage must increase; UNESCO will continue to support national technical teams in charge of the development or implementation of "National ESD Initiatives", with the support of all development actors. Faced with various issues related to sustainable development, such as poverty, inequality, insecurity and conflict, environmental degradation and climate change, the countries of the sub-region are aware of the urgent need for action, based on the youth and dynamism of their populations, and the resilience of their education and training systems. The choice was made to maintain the dynamic of collaboration between the countries of the sub-region with a view to their qualitative participation in global level events organized in the framework of education for sustainable development. During the 2024-2025 biennium, UNESCO engaged these States in a process of mutual capacity building and peer learning on themes related to Education for Sustainable Development. Countries in the sub-region participate in the regular webinars and training activities offered by the ESD-Net Network for 2030; their delegates interact: they met, among other things, at a sub-regional meeting organized by the Dakar Office in June 2025; they took part in the (online) meeting on ESD convened for National Technical Teams and ESD partners from Central and West Africa in December 2025. Following these events, recommendations were formulated, accompanied by a Joint Action Plan, at the national or subregional level. UNESCO is committed to continue sharing experiences, in particular regarding the development process of the National ESD Initiative for 2030, to offer its support for the development of capacities to analyse financing opportunities and mobilize domestic or external resources. For the 2026-2027 biennium, UNESCO will continue to support countries in identifying and formulating priority interventions that should be carried out before the 2030 deadline, with the support of various ESD actors and partners. Key activities to be conducted include: Support to the ESD process in the sub-region; Participation in the implementation of the educational program of the "Mangal Festival in Benin"; Support to countries to participate in the Global Conference on ESD.
